"They went back for him, and got him off safe, telling him nothing. But when he found she was dead he went crazy-like--kept for ever saying, 'She saved my life, she saved my life,' till he was taken away by his friends. Look out, ma'am, mind your footing; just here a lady slipped and broke her leg a week ago. I had to carry her all the way to the hotel. I shouldn't like to carry you." We all smiled at the comical candour of the honest sailor, who proceeded to give us bits of his autobiography. He was Cornish born, but had seen a deal of the world as an A.B. on board her Majesty's ship _Agamemnon_. "Of course you have heard of the _Agamemnon_, ma'am. I was in her off Balaklava.
